The ion enters from point B along the direction BC, that is, the initial velocity is horizontally to the right. A positive ion in a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward is subject to the Lorentz force, and at the instant of entry the direction of the force points toward above side AB, so the center of the circular motion is on line AB and above point B. The angular velocity of circular motion in a uniform magnetic field is ω=qB/m. If this ion finally exits from boundary AB, then its second intersection point with the straight line AB is the point on the circle opposite point B with respect to the center, so what it has traversed in the magnetic field is a semicircle, and the central angle is π. method.method_draft: Use the diagram to note that AB is perpendicular to BC and that the ion enters at B along BC, while AB is the vertical boundary through B. From the text, the magnetic field is uniform into the page and the ion is positive, so it executes uniform circular motion with cyclotron angular speed \(\omega=qB/m\). The Lorentz force at entry points toward AB, so the circle center lies on AB above B. If the particle finally exits through AB, its second intersection with the line AB occurs at the point diametrically opposite B on that circle, so the trajectory inside the field is a semicircle. Therefore the swept central angle is \(\pi\), and the time is \(t=\pi/\omega=\pi m/(qB)\).

method.method_draft: Set coordinates from the diagram: take B as the origin, BC as the positive x-axis, and AB as the y-axis. From the text, the positive ion enters with speed \(v\) along +x in a uniform field into the page, so its cyclotron motion has radius \(r=mv/(qB)\) and angular speed \(\omega=qB/m\). The coordinate form of the circular motion is \(x(t)=r\sin(\omega t)\), \(y(t)=r[1-\cos(\omega t)]\). To exit through AB, the particle must reach the line AB again, i.e. \(x(t)=0\), after entering. The first nonzero solution is \(\omega t=\pi\). Hence \(t=\pi/\omega=\pi m/(qB)\).
